Students combine academic study with applied projects, practical training and preparation for professional development in software engineering, computing and related technology fields. Why choose Software Systems and Technologies at VUM? Strong technical foundation: Students develop knowledge and skills in programming, software design, data structures and algorithms, computer architectures, operating systems, networks, databases, web and mobile technologies, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence and software quality assurance. Applied and industry-oriented learning: The programme combines theoretical knowledge with practical exercises, project work and authentic problem-solving activities designed to reflect real software engineering and technology challenges. Industry-informed teaching: Many lecturers are active professionals in the technology sector and bring current industry practices, technologies and real-world perspectives into the learning experience. Study schedule compatible with employment: The programme is delivered in full-time mode, with classes scheduled predominantly from 18:00 to 21:00 on weekdays and from 09:00 to 16:00 on Saturdays, allowing many students to combine their studies with work. Opportunity to earn a British degree in Bulgaria: Eligible full-time students may study towards both an accredited Bulgarian Professional Bachelor degree from VUM and the British BSc (Hons) Software Engineering awarded by Cardiff Metropolitan University. Career opportunities: The programme prepares students for careers in software development, software engineering, web and mobile application development, software testing and quality assurance, cybersecurity, data technologies, systems analysis, IT project support and related digital fields. apply online Key Facts Programme Software Systems and Technologies Mode of study Full-time Language of instruction English Degree awarded by VUM Professional Bachelor’s degree International award option Cardiff Metropolitan University degree available for eligible students in the final year Cardiff Met final award BSc (Hons) Software Engineering Practical training Summer internships during the programme Location Varna University of Management, Bulgaria Intakes Route September Intake February Intake Professional Bachelor 3 years / 6 semesters 3.5 years / 6 semesters *February-intake students complete the same number of semesters over a slightly longer calendar period, allowing their studies to align with the programme’s standard September progression cycle, including the final-year Cardiff Met top-up route. Programme Details Curriculum Select year of intake Professional Bachelor – 6 semesters Intake 2026-27 Intake 2025-26 Intake 2024-25 * Curricula may vary depending on the year of admission. Applicants and students should consult the curriculum applicable to their intake. * Please note that elective modules and additional credit-bearing optional modules are subject to availability and student demand; therefore, not all such modules may be offered in every academic year. Additional optional modules may carry credits but do not count towards the required credits for the degree. Admission Requirements Admission to VUM is based on the applicant’s educational background, academic performance, motivation, English language proficiency and submission of the required application documents. The admission process is carried out in accordance with VUM’s admission rules and the applicable Bulgarian legislation. Additional requirements may apply depending on the applicant’s citizenship, educational background, chosen mode of study and, where applicable, progression to the Cardiff Met final-year option. Applicants with documents issued outside Bulgaria may also be required to complete recognition, legalisation and translation procedures. View Admission Requirements and Application Steps Tuition Fees, Scholarships and Student Loans You can find detailed information about scholarship opportunities, semester tuition fees and student loans here . Cardiff Met Degree - Key Information The Cardiff Met top-up route is delivered at VUM in Bulgaria in the final year and is subject to meeting the applicable academic, English language, administrative and assessment requirements of both institutions. How the Cardiff Met Top-up Route Works The Cardiff Met option is available only in Year 3 of the full-time programme. During Years 1 and 2, students are enrolled at VUM and follow the VUM curriculum. Students may be considered for registration with Cardiff Metropolitan University in Year 3 only after they have successfully completed the required VUM studies and met the applicable academic, English language and progression requirements. Admission Policy and Procedures for Cardiff Met Programmes at VUM Credits and Final Award The Cardiff Met top-up route follows Cardiff Metropolitan University’s model for modular degrees. To receive an honours degree, students must successfully complete a total of 360 British credit points. As this is a one-year top-up route, students who have successfully completed the required VUM curriculum for Years 1 and 2 are normally eligible for recognition for 240 British credit points through Cardiff Met’s applicable Accreditation of Prior Learning procedures. They then complete the final-year modules worth 120 British credit points at VUM. The final-year comprises the following Cardiff Met modules: Module British Credit Points Parallel & Distributed Computing 20 Cyber Security & Cryptography 20 Advanced Programming 20 Professional, Sustainable & Ethical Technology 20 Development Project 40 Total final-year credit points 120 Final Award: BSc (Hons) Software Engineering * Disclaimer: Programme structures, modules learning activities and assessment requirements may change due to academic, regulatory, validation-related or operational reasons. VUM makes every effort to keep website information accurate and up to date; however, applicants are advised to request the latest programme information during the application process. Student Mobility VUM students have opportunities to take part in international mobility for study or traineeships. Students may spend a semester or academic year at one of VUM’s partner universities or complete traineeships with partner employers abroad, where applicable and subject to Erasmus+ rules and selection procedures. VUM works with more than 100 partner universities in over 20 countries and has long-standing partnerships with nearly 200 employers across Europe. For full-time students, traineeships are an important part of the study experience and are recognised towards the degree. Within the full educational cycle, students may take part in outgoing mobilities with a combined duration of up to 12 months. You can find detailed information about Erasmus+ study and traineeship opportunities here Career Development The Software Systems and Technologies programme is designed to support students’ professional development and preparation for careers in software engineering, computing and related technology fields. Graduates of the programme may pursue careers in areas such as: software development and software engineering; web and mobile application development; software testing and quality assurance; cybersecurity and information security; data management and data technologies; systems analysis and IT consulting; IT project coordination and technology operations; technology entrepreneurship and digital product development. Typical professional roles may include software developer, software engineer, web developer, mobile application developer, software tester, quality assurance specialist, junior cybersecurity specialist, systems analyst, database or data specialist, IT project coordinator or technology entrepreneur.
